rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says al-ʿafw originally means increase or surplus, as in taking what is extra or people becoming more numerous.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : أصل العفو في اللغة الزيادة ، قال تعالى

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl defines al-ʿafw as what is easy and available beyond one's sufficiency; Rāzī relates surplus to ease and removal of hardship.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : العفو ما سهل وتيسر مما يكون فاضلا عن الكفاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains the commanded expenditure as what remains beyond the needs of oneself, dependents, and those whose upkeep is one's responsibility.
rows.anchor: فالغالب أن ذلك إنما يكون فيما يفضل عن حاجة الإنسان في نفسه وعياله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spending command steers between wasteful generosity and miserliness, echoing commands to support kin and travelers, avoid waste, and spend without excess or stinginess.
rows.anchor: أدب الناس في الإنفاق فقال تعالى لنبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the exemption from alms on horses and slaves lightens the obligation; instead, a quarter-tenth of other wealth is due.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( عفوت لكم عن صدقة الخيل والرقيق فهاتوا ربع عشر أموالكم )

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says a person with something should begin with himself, then those he supports, proceeding outward in that order.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إذا كان عند أحدكم شيء فليبدأ بنفسه ، ثم بمن يعول وهكذا وهكذا )

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet calls the best charity what leaves its giver self-sufficient, and says a person with only enough for bare needs is not blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وقال / عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( خير الصدقة ما أبقت غني ولا يلام على كفاف )

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet angrily took a man's gold egg, his only wealth, threw it away, and said charity should come from abundance, not leave its giver begging.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر بن عبد الله قال بينما نحن عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، إذ جاءه رجل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet kept a year's provision for his family, illustrating the need to reserve enough for dependents.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يحبس لأهله قوت سنة

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The sages place virtue between excess and deficiency: lavish giving is waste, extreme parsimony is miserliness, and balance is the mean intended here.
rows.anchor: وقال الحكماء : الفضيلة بين طرفي الإفراط والتفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says Muḥammad's law balances these matters, unlike the Jews' complete severity and Christians' complete leniency, and is therefore more complete.
rows.anchor: فشرع اليهود مبناه على الخشونة التامة ، وشرع النصارى على المسامحة التامة ، وشرع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم متوسط في كل هذه الأمور

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads al-ʿafw with nominative wāw, parsing mā as a relative pronoun and the question as “what is it that they spend?”; others read it accusative as the answer “they spend the surplus.”
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ( العفو ) بضم الواو والباقون بالنصب

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says al-ʿafw may mean obligatory alms: the verse states the obligation generally while its details are given in the Sunna.
rows.anchor: قول أبي مسلم يجوز أن يكون العفو هو الزكاة فجاء ذكرها ههنا على سبيل الإجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another obligatory-spending view dates the command before the alms verse: people kept a year's needs and gave the remainder; the later alms verse abrogated it.
rows.anchor: أن هذا كان قبل نزول آية الصدقات فالناس كانوا مأمورين بأن يأخذوا من مكاسبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative view takes the spending as voluntary charity: because God leaves its amount to the addressee's judgment, it cannot be obligatory.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من هذا الإنفاق هو الإنفاق على سبيل التطوع وهو الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that God can impose a general obligation first and explain its details elsewhere, so lack of an amount here does not disprove obligation.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن يوجب الله شيئا على سبيل الإجمال ، ثم يذكر تفصيله وبيانه بطريق آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has clarified the kinds and destinations of spending asked about and will likewise explain all that people need in the days ahead.
rows.anchor: بينت لكم الأمر فيما سألتم عنه من وجوه الإنفاق ومصارفه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan proposes fronting and postponement: “in this world and the next” belongs with God's explaining the signs, before the purpose clause “so that you reflect.”
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : فيه تقديم وتأخير ، والتقدير : كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs teach that wine and gambling bring worldly benefits but afterlife harms; reflection should lead people to prefer the next life over this one.
rows.anchor: فيعرفكم أن الخمر والميسر فيهما منافع في الدنيا ومضار في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also invites reflection on giving wealth for the afterlife versus retaining it for worldly life, which should again yield preference for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أن إنفاق المال في وجوه الخير لأجل الآخرة وإمساكه لأجل الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects al-Ḥasan's fronting because the straightforward readings preserve the apparent word order, and no evidence requires departing from it.
rows.anchor: فرض التقديم والتأخير على ما قاله الحسن يكون عدولا عن الظاهر لا لدليل وأنه لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse supplies “We send him”: Jesus is taught the scriptures and then sent as a messenger to Israel, saying that he has brought a sign.
rows.anchor: تقدير الآية : ونعلمه الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل ونبعثه رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj prefers supplying “he speaks to people as a messenger”; the phrase that follows gives the content of Jesus' speech to them.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : الاختيار عندي أن تقديره : ويكلم الناس رسولا ، وإنما أضمرنا ذلك لقوله

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash allows the conjunction wāw to be extra, making “messenger to the Children of Israel” describe Jesus after the mention of his teachings.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش : إن شئت جعلت الواو زائدة ، والتقدير : ويعلمه الكتاب والحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī takes the verse to make Jesus a messenger to all the Children of Israel, contrary to some Jews' claim that he was sent only to a particular group.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان رسولا إلى كل بني إسرائيل بخلاف قول بعض اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A sign” means the class of signs, not one individual sign, since the verse lists raising the dead, healing, and disclosure of unseen matters.
rows.anchor: المراد بالآية الجنس لا الفرد لأنه تعالى عدد ههنا أنواعا من الآيات

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza opens the hamza in innī, making the clause “I create” an apposition explaining the sign Jesus brought.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة { إنى } بفتح الهمزة ، وقرأ نافع

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ breaks the hamza; the clause may either begin a new sentence or explain what the sign is.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع بكسر الهمزة فمن فتح { إنى } فقد جعلها بدلا من آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the broken-hamza reading, Rāzī prefers treating the clause as an explanation of the sign, parallel to explanatory clauses in 48:29 and 3:59; this matches the open reading's sense.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه أحسن لأنه في المعنى كقراءة من فتح { إنى } على جعله بدلا من آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī argues that khalq here means forming and measuring: humans do not create ex nihilo, “best of creators” means best estimators, and other verses use the root for fabricating lies.
rows.anchor: الذي يدل عليه القرآن والشعر والاستشهاد ، أما القرآن فآيات أحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “created” in 2:29 meant bringing into existence, it would say everything on earth had already been created in the past; Rāzī therefore takes it as prior measuring of what now exists.
rows.anchor: فإذن وجب حمل الخلق على التقدير حتى يصح الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī cites two poetic lines as evidence for shaping or measuring in khalq; the excerpt names no poet.
rows.anchor: ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبع ض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic usage supports measuring and smoothing: one shapes a sandal to size; khallāq is a measure of good, khalīq denotes a due measure, and smooth rock is called khalqāʾ.
rows.anchor: يقال : خلق النعل إذا قدرها وسواها بالقياس والخلاق المقدار من الخير

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله البصري
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Baṣrī denies that al-Khāliq is literally a divine name, since estimation and adjustment would mean conjecture, which is impossible for God.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله البصري : إنه لا يجوز إطلاقه على الله في الحقيقة ، لأن التقدير والتسوية عبارة عن الظن والحسبان

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Rāzī's theological school says al-Khāliq belongs only to God, citing “God is creator of everything” and “Is there any creator besides God who provides?”
rows.anchor: وقال أصحابنا : الخالق ، ليس إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says 35:3 alone does not prove that no one is a creator: it denies a creator other than God who has the specified role of providing from heaven.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف ، لأنه تعالى قال : { هل من خالق غير الله يرزقكم من السماء }

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: In response to al-Baṣrī, Rāzī's school says estimation can mean knowledge; conjecture is impossible for God, but knowledge is not.
rows.anchor: وأجابوا عن كلام أبي عبد الله بأن التقدير والتسوية عبارة عن العلم والظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse “I create” means “I form and measure”; hayʾa is the formed image, from the verb meaning to prepare or shape.
rows.anchor: { أنى أخلق لكم من الطين } معناه : أصور وأقدر وقوله { كهيئة الطير } فالهيئة الصورة المهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “I breathe into it” refers to the shaped clay.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فأنفخ فيه } أي في ذلك الطين المصور

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads the resulting bird in the singular; the other readers have the plural, as at 5:110, while ṭayr can denote one bird or many.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع { فيكون } بالألف على الواحد ، والباقون { عليهم طيرا } على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is narrated that when Jesus claimed prophethood, challengers demanded a bat; he fashioned and breathed into clay, and it flew between heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: يروى أن عيسى عليه السلام لما ادعى النبوة ، وأظهر المعجزات أخذوا يتعنتون عليه

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says the bird flew while people could see it but fell dead once it disappeared from their sight.
rows.anchor: قال وهب : كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون إليه ، فإذا غاب عن أعينهم سقط ميتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some said Jesus made only a bat, matching Nāfiʿ's reading; others said he made several kinds of bird, matching the other readers' plural.
rows.anchor: ثم اختلف الناس فقال قوم : إنه لم يخلق غير الخفاش ، وكانت قراءة نافع عليه

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
rows.claim: Some theologians infer from the breath that the spirit is a subtle body like wind.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المتكلمين : الآية تدل على أن الروح جسم رقيق كالريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says God, not Jesus' breath, created life in the clay as a miracle: only God gives life and death, as 67:2 and Abraham's argument in 2:258 show.
rows.anchor: وهذا الثاني هو الحق لقوله تعالى : { الذي خلق الموت والحيواة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' own birth was through Gabriel's breath into Mary; since Gabriel is pure spirit, Rāzī says Jesus' breath likewise concerned life and spirit.
rows.anchor: القرآن دل على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام إنما تولد من نفخ جبريل عليه السلام في مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “By God's permission” means God's bringing into being, as in 3:145; Jesus adds the phrase to ward off suspicions of divinity and identify life as God's miracle through a messenger.
rows.anchor: قوله { بإذن الله } معناه بتكوين الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Most lexicographers say al-akmah is someone born blind.
rows.anchor: ذهب أكثر أهل اللغة إلى أن الأكمه هو الذي ولد أعمى

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl and other authorities instead define al-akmah as someone who became blind after having sight.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل وغيره هو الذي عمي بعد أن كان بصيرا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says al-akmah means someone who cannot see at night.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد هو الذي لا يبصر بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī notes a claim that the only akmah in this community was Qatāda b. Diʿāma al-Sadūsī, the Qur'an commentator.
rows.anchor: ويقال : إنه لم يكن في هذه الأمة أكمه غير قتادة بن دعامة السدوسي صاحب ( التفسير )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says fifty thousand sick people gathered around Jesus; those able came to him, while he visited those unable to come, and treated them only by prayer.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ربما اجتمع عليه خمسون ألفا من المرضى من أطاق منهم أتاه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says Jesus raised Lazarus with “O Living, O Self-subsisting,” called Sām b. Noah from his grave, and revived an old woman's dead son, who returned home and had a child.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي : كان عيسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated qualification “by God's permission” removes the suspicion that Jesus is divine.
rows.anchor: وقوله { بإذن الله } رفع لتوهم من اعتقد فيه الإلاهية

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī reports that Jesus foretold children's deeds and hidden food while playing; parents hid the children, lied that the house held pigs, and Jesus said they would be pigs, whereupon they became so.
rows.anchor: روى السدي : أنه كان يلعب مع الصبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view says Jesus' disclosures began when the table descended: the people had been forbidden to store food but were hiding provisions.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : إن الإخبار عن الغيوب إنما ظهر وقت نزول المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unassisted foreknowledge without prior questions or instruments is a miracle from God; astrologers need questions and tools and still admit frequent error.
rows.anchor: الإخبار عن الغيوب على هذا الوجه معجزة ، وذلك لأن المنجمين الذين يدعون استخراج الخير

words: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These five powerful signs establish the claimant's truth for anyone who accepts miracles as proof; Brahmins reject that premise, but believers have no remaining objection.
rows.anchor: في هذه الخمسة لمعجزة قاهرة قوية دالة على صدق المدعي لكل من آمن بدلائل المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After directing spouses to treat one another well and end quarrels, God turns to ten further kinds of good conduct.
rows.anchor: لما أرشد كل واحد من الزوجين إلى المعاملة الحسنة مع الآخر وإلى إزالة الخصومة والخشونة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the command to worship God as a command to affirm His oneness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المعنى وحدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī defines worship as every act or omission done solely in response to God's command, including deeds of the heart and body; it is not limited to monotheism.
rows.anchor: العبادة عبارة عن كل فعل وترك يؤتى به لمجرد أمر الله تعالى بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on associating partners commands sincerity: worshipping another alongside God is incompatible with exclusive devotion, as 98:5 says.
rows.anchor: لأن من عبد مع الله غيره كان مشركا ولا يكون مخلصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ellipses an imperative, “do good to parents”; Rāzī compares “striking the necks” in 47:4, meaning “strike them.”
rows.anchor: واتفقوا على أن ههنا محذوفا ، والتقدير : وأحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: The poet Kathīr's line using aḥsin demonstrates the Arabic construction of doing good to someone.
rows.anchor: قال كثير : أسيئى بنا أو أحسنى لا ملومة لدنيا ولا مقلية إن تقلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeatedly joins kindness to parents with worship and monotheism—in this verse, 17:23, and 31:14—showing the weight of their rights.
rows.anchor: قرن إلزام بر الوالدين بعبادته وتوحيده في مواضع : أحدها : في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command includes not saying “uff,” not rebuking parents, and speaking graciously (17:23); even unbelieving parents merit good companionship, though one must not obey a call to shirk (31:15).
rows.anchor: فلا تقل لهما أف ولا تنهرهما وقل لهما قولا كريما

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports that a man from Yemen sought the Prophet's permission to join jihad; told to ask his parents, he had not, so the Prophet ordered him to return and honor them unless they permitted him to fight.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه : أن رجلا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindness to parents means serving them, speaking gently without raised voices, meeting their needs and supporting them as able, and not threatening or killing them.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الإحسان إلى الوالدين هو أن يقوم بخدمتهما ، وألا يرفع صوته عليهما

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī allows killing a parent only if leaving them alive would let them kill the child; otherwise enabling one's own death is forbidden self-destruction.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الرازي : إلا أن يضطر إلى ذلك بأن يخاف أن يقتله أن ترك قتله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet forbade Ḥanẓala b. Abī ʿĀmir al-Rāhib from killing his unbelieving father.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى حنظلة بن أبي عامر الراهب عن قتل أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Near kin” commands maintaining family ties, as the opening of the sūra also commands.
rows.anchor: وهو أمر بصلة الرحم كما ذكر في أول السورة بقوله : { والأرحام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parents are kin too, but birth-kin are singled out before other relatives because this is the closest relation and has special rights.
rows.anchor: لما كانت مخصوصة بكونها أقرب القرابات وكانت مخصوصة بخواص لا تحصل في غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphans suffer both childhood and lack of a provider, leaving them especially helpless and deserving of compassion.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن اليتيم مخصوص بنوعين من العجز : أحدهما : الصغر ، والثاني : عدم المنفق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says to treat orphans gently, raise them and stroke their heads; a guardian should carefully protect their property.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يرفق بهم ويربيهم ويمسح رأسهم ، وإن كان وصيا لهم فليبالغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the poor lack wealth, an adult can present his case to others to gain benefit or avert harm; an orphan cannot, which is why orphans are mentioned first.
rows.anchor: فلهذا المعنى قدم الله اليتيم في الذكر على المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindness to a poor person may mean giving generously or refusing courteously, as the command not to rebuff a petitioner says in 93:10.
rows.anchor: والإحسان إلى المسكين إما بالإجمال إليه ، أو بالرد الجميل . كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the near neighbor as one whose home is close and the distant neighbor as one whose home is farther away.
rows.anchor: قيل : هو الذي قرب جواره ، والجار الجنب هو الذي بعد جواره .

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that a person whose neighbor is unsafe from his harms will not enter Paradise; neighborliness extends forty homes.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( لا يدخل الجنة من لا يأمن جاره بوائقه ألا وإن الجوار أربعون دارا )

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī specifies forty neighbor homes in each of the four directions: right, left, front, and behind.
rows.anchor: وكان الزهري يقول : أربعون يمنة ، وأربعون يسرة ، وأربعون أماما وأربعون خلفا .

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A woman who fasted and prayed but verbally harmed neighbors was condemned by the Prophet as having no good and being destined for Hell.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة قيل : يا رسول الله ان فلانة تصوم النهار

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report lists neighborly duties: support a poor neighbor, lend on request, congratulate good fortune, console hardship, visit illness, and attend the funeral; few meet these duties.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( والذي نفس محمد بيده لا يؤدي حق الجار إلا من رحم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the near neighbor as a blood relative and the distant neighbor as a non-relative outsider.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : عني بالجار ذي القربى : القريب النسيب ، وبالجار الجنب : الجار الأجنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading puts dhā in the accusative as an emphatic specification, highlighting the neighbor's greater claim through both adjacency and kinship; Rāzī compares 2:238.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( والجار ذا القربى ) نصبا على الاختصاص ، كما قرىء ( حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى )
